---
title: "MuData as a standard data format"
description: "The core data format used by OpenPipelines."

---

The core data format used by OpenPipelines is the [MuData](https://mudata.readthedocs.io/) object.
All components read and write this format, providing interoperability and [modularity](modularity.qmd) throughout workflows.

MuData is the multimodal extension of [AnnData](https://anndata.readthedocs.io).
Within a MuData object, each modality is stored as an AnnData object under the `.mod` slot.
Inside a modality, expression matrices are stored in `.X` and `.layers`, cell metadata is stored in `.obs`, and feature metadata in `.var`.
Other fields store additional information, including cross-modality annotations.

```text
MuData
├─ .mod
│  ├─ rna  (AnnData)
│  │   ├─ .X          # expression matrix
│  │   ├─ .layers     # alternative matrices
│  │   ├─ .obs / .var # cell & feature annotation
│  │   └─ .obsm/.varm # embeddings, loadings
│  └─ prot (AnnData)
├─ .obs   # cross-modality cell annotation (e.g. sample_id)
└─ .var
```

## Anatomy of the object

Each slot has a fixed meaning, and the same slots exist both per-modality (inside
each AnnData under `.mod`) and at the top level (across modalities):

- **`.mod`**: the array of AnnData objects, one per modality
  (`rna`, `prot`, `atac`, `vdj_t`, …).
- **`.X` and `.layers`**: the measurement matrices. Columns are variables
  (genes/features), rows are observations (cells). `.layers` holds alternative
  versions of the same matrix (e.g. raw counts vs. normalized).
- **`.var`**: metadata for the variables (annotation for the columns of `.X`).
  One row per feature.
- **`.obs`**: metadata for the observations (annotation for the rows of `.X`).
  One row per cell. At the top level, `.obs` holds cross-modality cell annotation
  such as `sample_id`.
- **`.varm` / `.obsm`**: multi-dimensional variable / observation annotations:
  key → matrix mappings aligned to features (`.varm`, e.g. PCA loadings) or cells
  (`.obsm`, e.g. embeddings like `X_pca`, `X_umap`).
- **`.uns`**: unstructured annotation, with no dimensional constraints (run
  parameters, color maps, and cluster metadata).

## Working with other formats

To enable interoperability with other ecosystems, OpenPipelines provides a series of conversion components.
These allow you to transform your data to the format needed to run an OpenPipelines workflow or to take the output from a workflow and convert it to the format needed for your downstream analysis.

Supported conversion formats include:

- [AnnData](https://anndata.readthedocs.io/)
- [Seurat](https://satijalab.org/seurat/)
- [TileDB](https://tiledb.com/)
- [10x Cell Ranger, Space Ranger, or Xenium Ranger outputs](https://www.10xgenomics.com/)
- [CosMx output (exported from AtoMx)](https://brukerspatialbiology.com/)
- [Element AVITI24 output](https://www.elementbiosciences.com/)
- [SpatialData](https://spatialdata.scverse.org/en/stable/)
- [SpatialExperiment](https://bioconductor.org/packages/SpatialExperiment/)

See the [Reference](../reference/index.qmd) for more details on specific conversion components.
